threads.gloss: take account of, attend to; call to account; appoint, put in charge

opens.note: paqad opens the book: the two censuses (1, 26) and the Levite counts (3–4) are built on it; later it turns to ‘call to account’ (14:18, 29).

payoffs.note: Levi again stands outside the account (1:47); the same rare ‘were not accounted’ returns for the second generation at 26:62.
paqad turns from counting to appointing: Aharon and his sons are 'put in charge' of their priesthood.
Levi is accounted for from a month old, not twenty: a devoted tribe, not an army, and the count must come out exact.
Counting turns to oversight and inventory: Elazar's oversight (4:16), appointments (4:27), and vessels accounted for by name (4:32).

opens.note: tsavaʾ, the fighting force Israel is accounted into; 4:3 reuses it for Levite service at the tent and 31 for the Midian campaign.

payoffs.note: The fighting-force word turned to Levite duty: they 'come into the army' to do work at the Tent of Meeting.

threads.gloss: community, assembly gathered as one body

opens.note: ʿedah, Israel as one assembled body; it becomes the actor that complains, rebels and is judged (14:1–2, 16:3, 20:1–2).

payoffs.note: The community owes the sanctuary's upkeep; the Levites keep its charge on its behalf.

threads.note: ʿedah, Israel as one assembled body; it becomes the actor that complains, rebels and is judged (14:1–2, 16:3, 20:1–2).

opens.note: qeriʾ, ‘called’: the called ones of the community (qeriʾe ha-ʿedah) are the chieftains at 16:2 and 26:9, where Korach’s company and Datan and Aviram are described by the title the chieftains bear in 1:16 (there a different form, qeruʾe).

payoffs.note: The second census recalls the same title for Datan and Aviram, ‘called of the community’ (26:9).

threads.gloss: charge, guard-duty, what one keeps watch over

opens.note: mishmeret, the Levites’ and priests’ ‘charge’ that structures chs. 3–4 and 18.

payoffs.note: mishmeret becomes the chapter's organizing noun: the Levites keep Aharon's charge and the whole community's.
The leaders camp at the east entrance 'keeping the charge of the holy place', the most exposed post in the camp.
Charge now names each house's load, assigned and supervised by the priests (4:27–33); Lev 8:35 tied keeping it to not dying.

threads.gloss: encamp; a camp, the body encamped

opens.note: ḥanah, to camp: first the Levites camp around the Dwelling as a cordon (1:50, 53); ch. 2 then orders the whole camp around it, and the camp’s purity and edge carry the book (5:2–4; 12:14–15; 14:44; 19:3).

payoffs.note: ḥanah / maḥaneh, the camp and its camping: the ordered space around the tent whose purity, edge and outside carry the book (5:2–4; 12:14–15; 14:44; 19:3).

threads.gloss: pull up stakes, set out, march

opens.note: nasaʿ, ‘set out’: first as the Levites’ duty to take the Dwelling down when it sets out (1:51); ch. 2 orders the march, and it is narrated at 10:11–36 and repeated at every station of ch. 33.

payoffs.note: The march order itself: ‘First they shall set out’ (2:9) begins the sequence of ranks.

opens.note: maṭṭeh, ‘tribe’ that is literally ‘staff’: first as the man for each tribe (1:4, 16); ch. 17’s twelve staffs turn on it, and 26, 34 and 36 allot the land by it.

threads.gloss: stranger, one not authorized; strange, unsanctioned

opens.note: zar, the one not authorized to approach: the cordon refrain first sounds here (1:51; again 3:10, 38); Korach’s censers (16:40) and ch. 18 return to it.

payoffs.note: Nadav and Avihu’s strange fire (3:4): zar and qarav together describe the offering that kills.

opens.note: qarav, the verb of legitimate presentation and lethal presumption alike: first the stranger who comes near is put to death (1:51); chs. 16–18 turn on who may draw near.

payoffs.note: Nadav and Avihu ‘brought near’ strange fire (3:4); in 3:6 the same verb presents Levi to Aharon.

threads.gloss: holy; set apart; the holy place

opens.note: qadash, qodesh, miqdash: the holiness that makes nearness dangerous, from the firstborn set apart to the holy place and its shekel.

payoffs.note: Holiness becomes a contact hazard: priests may touch, Levites may only carry, and no one may look (4:15, 20).

opens.note: ‘By the number of names’: the count of persons that frames both censuses.

payoffs.note: The Levite clans counted by the same formula.
A ‘number of days’ under the cloud.
‘All your accounted ones, by your whole number’ fall in the wilderness; 14:34 sets the number of days to years.
Offerings scaled ‘by the number’ of animals.
Balaam: who has numbered a fourth of Yisrael?
The land divided ‘by the number of names’ — the formula of 1:2 returns.
The festival offerings ‘by their number’: the sense drifts to a tally of animals.
The Midian spoil divided by number.

threads.note: mispar, the count itself; 34 occurrences. In chs. 15 and 29 it tallies offerings, not persons.
